key_insight: Thermodynamics-informed input reparameterization (TAIR) makes neural surrogates easier to learn by replacing raw enthalpy with target-matched ideal-gas thermodynamic coordinates, so the network focuses on real-fluid deviations rather than reconstructing the full closure from scratch.
engineering_relevance: TAIR can cut the cost of thermodynamic property evaluation in supercritical combustion solvers while improving accuracy, making data-driven closures more practical for high-fidelity reacting-flow simulation.
method: Temperature network: replace enthalpy with an ideal-gas constant-cp inversion-based temperature estimate.
Density and compressibility networks: replace enthalpy with an ideal-gas density estimate.
Train target-aligned surrogates to predict real-fluid T, ρ, and ψ as departures from these thermodynamic baselines.
evidence_signal: On supercritical methane-oxygen counterflow flame data, TAIR reduced held-out RMSE by about 1.5× for T, 2.0× for ρ, and 7.5× for ψ, and generalized to an unseen strain-rate flame with gains of 3.6×, 14.5×, and 6.0×.
watch_item: Performance depends on having a thermodynamically consistent reparameterization; mismatched target controls perform worse, so the chosen baseline must align with the predicted property and solver assumptions.
paper_title: Thermodynamics-Informed Input Reparameterization for Neural Prediction of Real-Fluid Thermodynamic Properties in Supercritical Combustion
